title: "XOR (Exclusive OR)"
description: "A logical operation that is true when its two binary inputs differ."
term: "XOR (Exclusive OR)"
letter: "X"
category: "Computer Science"
difficulty: "Beginner"
---

## Simple explanation

XOR, or exclusive OR, outputs true when exactly one of two inputs is true.
For example, $0\oplus1=1$, while $1\oplus1=0$.

## Technical explanation

For binary values, XOR is addition modulo two: $a\oplus b=(a+b)\bmod 2$.
It is a Boolean operation used in digital circuits, checksums, and
cryptographic constructions. XOR is associative and commutative and satisfies
$a\oplus a=0$.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

XOR is a foundational example in machine learning: a single linear
threshold unit cannot represent the XOR truth table, while a network with a
hidden layer and nonlinear activation can. It also appears in low-level
systems and data transformations.

## How it works

Evaluate the two inputs and return one when they differ, zero when they match.
For bit strings, apply the operation independently to each corresponding bit.

## Practical example

The XOR function can test whether two binary flags disagree. As a learning
problem, it illustrates why nonlinear representations are necessary for some
decision boundaries.

## Common misconceptions

- XOR is not ordinary OR: OR returns true when both inputs are true, whereas
  XOR does not.
- The classic XOR limitation applies to a single linear decision unit, not to
  all neural networks.
